data.claim: ddflow/api/cirun.py:_keep_failing_ids records only failing_ids_note and does not write the failing_ids blob when a non-test check fails beside red tests, so gate_baseline._ci_ids cannot recover the ids and the red tests are never measured on the base
data.falsifier: a direct call of _keep_failing_ids with a Result failing 'ruff check' plus red tests returns a dict WITHOUT a failing_ids key (only failing_ids_note)
data.mechanism: the 'if not BL.only_tests_failed(res.checks)' branch stores a 'not kept' note instead of the blob that BL.read_full reads back
data.probe: python call constructing Result(status=failed, checks=[Check('ruff check',False), Check('unit tests + end-to-end scenarios',False)], failures={'failed_tests':['tests/test_x.py::test_a']}); then BL.read_full on the returned blob
data.probe_output: after the fix it returns failing_ids and read_full recovers ['tests/test_x.py::test_a']; before the fix it returned only failing_ids_note
data.question: Does a ci run that fails with BOTH a non-test check and red tests keep the failing test ids aside, so the baseline of those tests can be measured on the base?

evidence.note: R4ffaaa760f CONFIRMED: _keep_failing_ids records only failing_ids_note and no failing_ids blob when a non-test check fails beside red tests, so _ci_ids cannot recover the ids; the fix keeps the blob regardless (direct python probe confirmed read_full recovers the id after the change).
